input_oneliner: 68F HTN and OSA, admitted for COPD exacerbation, woke with racing irregular heartbeat, HR 130s on tele, BP 132/84, no chest pain

optional_context.comorbidity: hypertension, obstructive sleep apnea, inpatient for COPD exacerbation

reference_targets_freetext.item: Radial pulse regularity and apical-radial pulse deficit (irregularly irregular rhythm)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Irregularly irregular pulse is the key bedside discriminator for AF versus regular tachycardias

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about abrupt versus gradual onset and whether the rate is fixed or fluctuates with activity
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: AF/SVT start abruptly; secondary sinus tachycardia builds gradually and varies with rest

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about rapid regular pounding in the neck / visible neck pulsations during episodes
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Neck pounding has a very high LR+ for AVNRT; its absence alongside an irregular pulse supports AF

reference_targets_freetext.item: Medication review (MAR): nebulized beta-agonist and steroid doses, missed beta-blocker; ask about alcohol and caffeine in the last 24 h
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: One precipitant-history question: reversible drivers of secondary sinus tachycardia and new-onset AF
Elevated JVP identifies decompensated HF as cause or consequence, changing the rate-control agent and urgency
Pulmonary congestion from rapid AF or underlying HF; supports urgency of rate control

reference_targets_freetext.item: Thyroid examination and signs of thyrotoxicosis: fine tremor, warm moist skin, lid lag
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Hyperthyroidism is a common reversible cause of new AF

should_not_recommend: Empiric IV rate control or adenosine before the pulse is examined and the rhythm confirmed on a 12-lead ECG
Adenosine for a rhythm that is irregularly irregular
Cardioversion before hemodynamic status and anticoagulation status are assessed
